messages:
carmen: Heads-up — new onboarding friction: `redwoodctl login --local-serve` failed for a new user on macOS. Browser opened to callback but CLI never got it (ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED).

lee: Ask which installer they used (brew vs pkg). Also `which redwoodctl`.

carmen: They used the signed pkg. `which` reported /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl but pkg installs to /opt/redwood/bin. Old binary was left behind.

ravi: Classic shadowing. Old binary might bind different port. We bumped callback port from 8085 to 8087 last release.

carmen: After removing old `/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` the browser showed a macOS firewall prompt and CLI errored: "Error: listen EACCES 0.0.0.0:8087". Allowing the app in Security & Privacy fixed it.

lee: Action items: 1) CLI should catch EACCES and print a macOS firewall hint. 2) Installer postinstall should detect multiple `redwoodctl` instances and warn. 3) Quickstart docs should mention `REDWOODCTL_DEVICE_CODE=1` for headless/CI auth.

ops-bot: CI: pre-release redwoodctl-0.9.2-alpha built (signed). https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/2360

ravi: I'll open small PRs for the EACCES hint and sample-app env alias (accept REDWOOD_API_URL as fallback). lee, can you add the postinstall PATH-scan to the pkg script?

lee: Yep. Filing issue and docs note now.

carmen: Thanks — once we surface clearer errors this will reduce onboarding tickets.
